solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Decadent English s-social function

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
a fete is a social function, and the printed stammer 's-social' tells you to stutter its first letter too

explanation.surface: An English social gathering dismissed as decadent, reported by someone stammering over the word.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 's-s' is not a typo: it models a stammer, so the synonym for the function is stammered in the same way, doubling its opening F.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete describes someone or something weak, over-refined and self-indulgent, which is close to decadent.

clue.text: Cactus intoxicant initially missing, devoured mushroom

indicators.note: what is missing at the start has lost its opening letter

blocks.note: mescal is the drug made from the peyote cactus
devoured means ate

explanation.surface: Someone skipped the cactus drug and ate a mushroom instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' looks like the thing that was eaten, but it is a verb meaning to grow rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or spread rapidly, and things that escalate increase quickly in size or intensity.

clue.text: Ornamental design to worry about and fashion

blocks.note: to fret is to worry about something
to work metal or wood is to fashion it; 'and' just joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A designer frets over an ornamental pattern and how fashionable it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' reads as a noun about style, but here it is the verb meaning to shape or make.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretwork is decorative carved or cut openwork in wood or metal, an ornamental pattern.

clue.text: Article softened set of principles

blocks.note: the definite article
to creed grain or rice is to soften it by boiling, a rare dictionary sense

explanation.surface: A newspaper article has been toned down, like a watered-down statement of beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece relies on an obscure verb: in Chambers, to creed rice or wheat is to soften it by boiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a formal statement of belief, a system of principles held by a church or group.

clue.text: Wild banshees are those who are past it

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Screaming Irish spirits dismissed as washed-up old performers.
explanation.walkthrough: A banshee is a wailing spirit of Irish folklore; the word's letters rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person whose fame or usefulness is over, someone no longer in their prime.

clue.text: Illustrator Beardsley is a new buyer

definitions.note: the answer is the illustrator's first name, not the whole name

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The famous illustrator turns out to be a first-time purchaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New buyer' reads as a phrase about a customer; 'new' is the signal to rearrange 'a buyer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubrey Beardsley was the Victorian black-and-white illustrator of Wilde's Salome, so his forename completes the phrase.

clue.text: Hardly like a nude!

blocks.note: first meaning: only just, scarcely
second meaning, read literally: in a bare way, unclothed

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into 'bare' plus the adverb ending, so it means 'in the manner of something bare'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means scarcely or only just, and read whimsically it also means in an unclothed manner, as a nude is.

clue.text: Say the sappers return and come into view

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, which is what 'say' means in 'say, a dog'
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army engineering corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers come back from an operation and appear over the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; the usual abbreviation is RE, but here the setter uses the longer REME.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out from hiding or become visible, which is coming into view.

clue.text: Menacing comic character turned up, having broken social bounds

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for a past-tense verb

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning something upwards reads it from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: Dennis the Menace is a mischievous boy in the British children's comic the Beano

explanation.surface: A troublemaking comic-strip figure appears after behaving outrageously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Menacing' points to the character's title, the Menace, rather than describing him.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to transgress moral rules, which is breaking the bounds of acceptable behaviour.

clue.text: Basket holding women’s yarn

indicators.note: whatever holds something else wraps round it

blocks.note: a creel is a wicker basket, as used for fish
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A knitting basket full of the ladies' wool.
explanation.walkthrough: A creel is best known as an angler's wicker basket for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a thin worsted wool used for embroidery and tapestry, a kind of yarn.

clue.text: City’s Lincoln Road is even shorter

indicators.note: a shorter word has lost part of itself, here a middle letter as in poetic contraction

blocks.note: Abe is the nickname of Abraham Lincoln
Rd is the abbreviation for road
taken as written before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A street named after Lincoln in some city turns out to be shorter still.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortening copies the poetic contraction e'en, which drops the V from the middle rather than the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city on the north-east coast of Scotland, known as the Granite City.

clue.text: Puts down cows, it could be said

blocks.note: first meaning: sets down, brings to a lower position
second meaning, a whimsical coinage: cows low, so they are things that low

explanation.surface: A farmer lays down the cows, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be said' flags that the second meaning is a playful invented noun rather than a dictionary word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something is to bring it down to a lower position, and mooing cattle could jokingly be called by the same word.

clue.text: Excited seeing leg, not small, in diaphanous garment

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order
S is the abbreviation for small, and 'not' says to leave it out

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets excited at a glimpse of leg through sheer nightwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the S of 'seeing', then rearrange what is left together with 'leg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light, often sheer woman's dressing gown, a see-through garment.

clue.text: Streamlined housing getting energy from sodium battery first

blocks.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a cell is a single battery unit
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An engine casing is powered by a sodium battery installed first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you the sodium battery comes before the energy, even though energy is named earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined casing on an aircraft that holds an engine, fuel or equipment.

clue.text: Bird from Germany — yes — with pretty tail

indicators.note: a tail is the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: ja is German for yes
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A German birdwatcher confirms a sighting of a bird with a lovely tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty tail' sounds like the bird's plumage, but it asks for the end of the word 'pretty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The jay is a noisy, colourful member of the crow family, a common bird in Europe.

clue.text: Blackened the reputation late over the Channel, it’s said

definitions.note: a verb phrase for the past-tense verb

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the sound counts

blocks.note: tard is French for late; France is across the Channel from Britain

explanation.surface: A reputation was ruined too late, across in France.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic English accent the answer sounds just like the French word for late.
explanation.definitionFit: To tar someone, as in tar with the same brush, is to smear and blacken their reputation.

clue.text: Made 501 with Durham opener

indicators.note: an opener is what starts things, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and I is 1
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricketer scored 501 opening the batting for Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is an English county cricket team, so 'opener' looks like an opening batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Did and made are both past tenses of verbs for carrying out or performing, as in did or made an effort.

clue.text: German grandma — a woman, at heart

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the three central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A German grandmother is at heart just an ordinary woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' means the middle of the word that follows, not a quality of character.
explanation.definitionFit: Oma is the familiar German word for grandmother, like granny in English.

clue.text: Difficulty turning cover on Austen’s work

indicators.note: something turning round faces the other way, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to turn the cover of a Jane Austen novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' puts the novel after the turned cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is an awkward situation requiring a hard choice, a difficulty or predicament.

clue.text: Chronicler or data specialist, we’re told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the sound matters

blocks.note: an analyst examines data in detail

explanation.surface: A historian or a data scientist, depending on whom you believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' offers the two readings: the written one is the definition, the spoken one is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, the year-by-year records of events, so is a chronicler.

clue.text: Prisoner rearranged date in Spain, twice

indicators.note: to rearrange is to put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España), used twice

explanation.surface: An inmate's release date is moved around while in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the four letters of 'date' are rearranged; the rest is added in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is a person held in custody, often without trial, which makes them a prisoner.

clue.text: Marine view with wild escapades without a touch of dignity

indicators.note: wild things are out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder
without means lacking, so a letter is taken away
a touch is only a small part, so just the opening letter is meant

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A painting of the sea shows sailors on undignified wild adventures.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the D from 'escapades', then shuffle the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a picture or view of the sea, and marine means relating to the sea.

clue.text: Adjoining building with a new name on river

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
N is the abbreviation for name
the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A riverside extension to a building has been given a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' means placed after, so the river comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building joined to or added onto a larger main building, the British spelling.

clue.text: Freelances — as a char?

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the answer's verb does, standing for the verb

indicators.note: set free, things break loose from their fixed order

blocks.note: split the word as two: after the signal word, the rest is taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-employed worker, perhaps a cleaning lady, taking jobs here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is hidden inside a single word: split it as 'Free lances'. A char, or charwoman, is British for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is paid to do housework, so doing what a char does means scrubbing and tidying homes.

clue.text: Favouring training? Right? Right!

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
PE is physical education, school exercise training
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone checks they are in favour of training, and is emphatically told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'Right's play different roles: the first is a letter, the exclaimed second one is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or appropriate, which is what 'right' means in the sense of fitting.

clue.text: Inwardly composed, at ease, calm

indicators.note: inwardly means on the inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: running across the words, ignoring the space and comma

explanation.surface: Someone who is serene inside: composed, at ease and calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The list of three near-synonyms makes 'composed' look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm, unhurried and dignified in manner, a close synonym.

clue.text: Length of US railroad

blocks.note: first meaning: an old measure of cloth length, about 45 inches
second meaning: Chicago's elevated railway, called the L, the letter's name spelt out

explanation.surface: A question about how long an American railway line is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Length of' tempts you to measure something, but the two phrases are independent meanings joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an archaic unit of measurement and the spelt-out name of the letter used for Chicago's elevated trains.

clue.text: Ancient Jew from German city quarter

blocks.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
E, for east, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: An ancient Jewish figure hails from a district of a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City quarter' reads as a neighbourhood, but a quarter is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the Second Temple period, linked with the Dead Sea Scrolls.

clue.text: Munificent gift of wafting eelgrass

indicators.note: wafting things drift about in the air, so the letters float into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A generous present of seaweed drifting in the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: Eelgrass is a seagrass that grows in shallow coastal water.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity in giving money or gifts, or the generous gift itself.

clue.text: Ask Katy about tenor having left canoes

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are turned into a new order
something that has left is no longer there, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: Ask Katy about the singer who left in the canoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from 'Ask Katy', then rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Kayaks are small enclosed canoes paddled with a double-bladed paddle.

clue.text: Transpired to have copied bearing fruit

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so one piece carries another inside it

blocks.note: to ape is to copy or mimic
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: It turned out that someone had imitated a tree producing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing fruit' is a set phrase for succeeding, but 'bearing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpired can mean came to light or turned out to be the case, which matches appeared, as in it appeared that.

clue.text: Reddish-brown pigment from church removed from Chennai’s rebuild

indicators.note: what is removed is taken out, so letters are lost
to rebuild is to put the parts together again in a new form

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
the city's name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A church in Chennai is rebuilt in a red-brown colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Chennai, formerly Madras, is an Indian city; its possessive S is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment containing iron oxide, raw sienna being yellow-brown and burnt sienna reddish-brown.

clue.text: Canvassed — used very crudely

indicators.note: something done crudely is rough and disordered, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter's canvas was treated very roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvassed' suggests canvas used crudely by an artist, but it is the opinion-poll sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass opinions is to poll people about their views, which is surveying them.

clue.text: Entertainer removed touch of paint from church spire

indicators.note: a touch is only a small part, so just the opening letter is used
removed means taken away, so a letter is lost from the longer word

blocks.note: a steeple is a church spire
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A performer scraped a speck of paint off a church spire.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Steele is a British singer and actor, an early British rock and roll star.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a category term: Tommy Steele is an example of an entertainer, a showbusiness performer.
